profiles.meeting_scenario: Riverton University is preparing a late-September 'Resilient Campus Week' initiative that is meant to improve disaster mitigation and response efficiency while also serving as an early Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) implementation effort. The initiative combines a flood-and-heatwave response exercise with teaching materials intended for selected first-year courses. This coordination meeting is between the university's operations-side resilience lead and the academic-side curriculum lead. The agenda is to align on the pilot launch, participant confirmations, the briefing pack and where it will be stored, and which campus flood map will be embedded in the materials. The expected outcome is a shared understanding of who hands off what by next week so both workstreams can proceed without delaying the launch.

members.name: Nina Alvarez
members.role: Director of Campus Resilience and Business Continuity
members.expertise: Emergency preparedness, incident command, continuity planning, multi-campus response exercises
members.background: Nina spent eight years in municipal emergency management before joining Riverton University to modernize its disaster readiness processes and coordinate cross-campus drills.
members.private_state: She wants the initiative to prove the resilience office can run a smooth, low-disruption exercise before storm season, and she is wary of academic add-ons creating delays or uncontrolled participation.
hidden_assumptions: A 'pilot' is a tightly controlled initial exercise with a limited number of staff representatives rather than a broad live rollout.
When participation is 'confirmed,' the important threshold is that each unit has named its operational representatives and safety contacts.
The 'shared site' for materials is the resilience SharePoint/Teams space already used for exercise injects and controller documents.
The standard 'downtown campus flood map' is the emergency GIS layer updated after the 2024 drainage redesign and building access changes.

members.name: Dr. Leo Chen
members.role: Associate Dean for Curriculum Innovation and Sustainability
members.expertise: Curriculum design, ESD integration, assessment design, faculty implementation support
members.background: Leo previously led interdisciplinary sustainability curriculum projects at two universities and was brought in to help Riverton embed resilience and sustainability capabilities into the student learning experience.
members.private_state: He wants the initiative to become a visible proof point that sustainability and disaster resilience can be embedded into ordinary teaching, and he needs enough real student-facing activity to justify future curriculum funding.
hidden_assumptions: A 'pilot' means a first live teaching implementation in selected courses, even if it is limited in scale.
When participation is 'confirmed,' the relevant threshold is that course sessions are timetabled and students will actually receive the activity.
The 'shared site' for materials is the academic LMS/teaching SharePoint where tutors and students can access the packet.
The usual 'downtown campus flood map' is the teaching visual from the urban resilience module that includes watershed context and community assets around the campus.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to getting the 'pilot' ready for late September.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks the pilot is a controlled operational exercise involving designated staff, controllers, and a small test of response procedures before wider use.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks the pilot is a live curricular rollout in three first-year courses where students complete the activity as part of their learning.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In universities, 'pilot' routinely means a limited first phase, so the shared word creates a strong sense of alignment even though each person silently imagines a different audience and scale.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree they need participation 'confirmed by Monday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes confirmation means each participating school or campus unit has named a staff controller and a safety contact for the exercise.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes confirmation means the relevant course leaders have locked the session into their teaching schedule and students will receive the materials.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are talking about a reasonable checkpoint called 'confirmation,' but each uses standards appropriate to their own workstream, and neither expects the other to define the term explicitly.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the briefing pack should be 'on the shared site by Thursday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 plans to upload an operations packet to the resilience Teams/SharePoint space, including facilitator notes, inject timings, and contact sheets.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 plans for a teaching packet to appear in the LMS-linked academic SharePoint, including the student brief, tutor guide, and reflection template.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Each side already has an established cross-team repository they casually call the shared site, and because putting files somewhere common sounds mundane, the assumed platform difference goes unnoticed.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'downtown campus flood map' goes in the briefing
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they will use 'the downtown campus flood map' in the materials.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the emergency GIS map showing current building entrances, evacuation paths, and the 2024 drainage changes on the downtown campus.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the sustainability teaching map used in the urban resilience module, which shows the campus in relation to the watershed and nearby community support assets.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both know that a familiar map exists under nearly the same label, and because the discussion stays at the level of 'including the map' rather than opening and inspecting it together, the reference mismatch feels too trivial to check.

turns.inner_thought: I need this late-September pilot to stay contained and well run: designated staff, controllers, safety contacts, no sprawling live rollout that complicates the exercise before storm season. If operations and teaching are lined up at the launch level, great, but I do not want academic extras slowing the exercise design or expanding the participant pool beyond a manageable first test.

turns.inner_thought: From my side, the pilot means the first live teaching implementation in a small set of courses during Resilient Campus Week. If we can get this into those first-year classes, we'll have a visible proof point that resilience and sustainability can live inside ordinary teaching, which will help the next funding conversation.
turns.utterance: Yes, from the curriculum side it still looks feasible. The first-year sustainability units are getting ready to use it as part of Resilient Campus Week, so the pilot timing still makes sense to me.

turns.inner_thought: The scenario injects and controller notes are basically there. What I really need now is confirmation that each participating unit has named its operational representative and safety contact by Monday, otherwise I can't lock the run sheet or keep the exercise controlled.
turns.utterance: Good. On our side, the scenario injects and controller notes are nearly done. The main thing I still need is to have participation confirmed by Monday so we can lock the last pieces down.

turns.inner_thought: Monday should be enough if the remaining course leaders commit. For me, confirmed participation means the sessions are actually timetabled and students will receive the activity, not just that someone is generally supportive. Two lecturers still need to finalize their teaching plans.

turns.inner_thought: Once we tidy the exercise packet, my team will upload it to the resilience SharePoint and Teams space we already use for injects, facilitator docs, and contact sheets. That way controllers and unit reps will all be working from the same operational version.
turns.utterance: Perfect. Once the final briefing pack is cleaned up, my team will put it on the shared site by Thursday so everyone is working from the same version.

turns.inner_thought: Thursday works. Before the pack goes onto the academic shared site tied to the LMS, I need to add the reflection sheet, tutor prompts, and the student-facing pieces so teaching staff can pick it up directly. That should make the classroom rollout smoother.
turns.utterance: Thursday is fine by me. I'll attach the reflection sheet and tutor prompts before the pack goes onto the shared site.

turns.inner_thought: We need the emergency GIS version of the downtown campus flood map in there, specifically the one updated after the 2024 drainage redesign, because route assumptions and building access have changed. People will need the current operational picture during the exercise.
turns.utterance: One thing I do want to make sure stays in the briefing is the downtown campus flood map, because people will need the latest route assumptions during the exercise.

turns.inner_thought: Agreed. The teaching map we use in the urban resilience module is ideal because it shows the watershed context and nearby community assets, which helps students connect campus risk to the wider system. That will strengthen the learning side without adding much overhead.
turns.utterance: Agreed, the downtown campus flood map works well. It already gives students enough context on watershed risk and nearby community assets.

turns.inner_thought: So my priorities are straightforward: finish the controlled pilot materials, post the operational pack to our resilience site by Thursday, and verify that each area has named the right people by Monday. If I can keep that sequence tight, we should avoid last-minute disruption.
turns.utterance: Great. Then on my side I'll finalize the pilot materials, post the pack on Thursday, and keep checking that each area has confirmed participation by Monday.

turns.inner_thought: I'll chase the remaining lecturers, fold the student-facing components into the teaching packet, and watch for the Thursday upload on the academic site so the classroom pilot can go live on time. If this lands well in late September, it gives me exactly the evidence I need for broader curriculum adoption.
